mcqs.question: In the equilibrium 2NO(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), the concentration of NO₂ is suddenly increased. According to Le Chatelier’s principle, what will be the shift in the position of equilibrium?

options.A: The equilibrium will shift to the right, producing more NO₂.
options.B: The equilibrium will shift to the left, forming more NO and O₂.
options.C: There will be no shift; the system is already at equilibrium.
options.D: The forward reaction will stop while the reverse reaction continues.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium will shift to the left, forming more NO and O₂.
mcqs.explanation: Adding NO₂ increases its concentration, creating a stress on the system. To oppose this change, the reaction shifts toward the reactants (left) to consume the added NO₂, restoring equilibrium. The forward reaction does not become favored; instead, the reverse reaction is favored. Options A and D describe opposite effects, and C ignores the disturbance.

mcqs.question: For the gaseous equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at constant temperature, the volume of the system is decreased, thereby increasing the total pressure. What is the expected shift in the equilibrium position?

options.A: The equilibrium shifts to the right, producing more NH₃.
options.B: The equilibrium shifts to the left, producing more N₂ and H₂.
options.C: There is no shift because pressure changes affect only the rate, not the position.
options.D: Both sides shift equally, so the composition remains unchanged.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium shifts to the right, producing more NH₃.
mcqs.explanation: Increasing pressure favors the side with fewer moles of gas. The left side has 4 moles (1 N₂ + 3 H₂) while the right side has 2 moles of NH₃. Hence the system shifts right to reduce pressure. Option B is opposite, C is false because pressure does affect position when mole numbers differ, and D misinterprets Le Chatelier’s principle.

mcqs.question: Consider two equilibria at 298 K: (1) N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) ΔH = –92 kJ (exothermic) and (2) CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g) ΔH = +178 kJ (endothermic). If the temperature is raised, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Both equilibria shift to the right.
options.B: Both equilibria shift to the left.
options.C: Equilibrium (1) shifts to the left, while equilibrium (2) shifts to the right.
options.D: Equilibrium (1) shifts to the right, while equilibrium (2) shifts to the left.

mcqs.answer: Equilibrium (1) shifts to the left, while equilibrium (2) shifts to the right.
mcqs.explanation: Raising temperature adds heat. For an exothermic reaction (ΔH < 0), heat is a product; the system counteracts by shifting left (absorbing heat). For an endothermic reaction (ΔH > 0), heat is a reactant; the system shifts right to consume the added heat. Hence statement C is correct. Options A and B ignore the sign of ΔH, and D reverses the correct directions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand effect of catalysts on equilibrium
mcqs.question: A catalyst is added to a reversible reaction that is already at equilibrium. Which of the following statements best describes its effect?

options.A: It increases the equilibrium constant (K) of the reaction.
options.B: It shifts the equilibrium position toward the products.
options.C: It speeds up the rate at which equilibrium is reached without changing K.
options.D: It decreases the rate of the forward reaction while leaving the reverse rate unchanged.

mcqs.answer: It speeds up the rate at which equilibrium is reached without changing K.
mcqs.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy, accelerating both forward and reverse reactions equally. Consequently, the system attains equilibrium faster, but the position of equilibrium and the equilibrium constant remain unchanged. Option A is false because K is a thermodynamic quantity, not kinetic. Option B misinterprets the effect as a shift. Option D incorrectly states asymmetric effect on rates.
